pulls.title: Remote Attestation Extensions for EST: review items, ProVerif model, reference implementation, hardware measurements
pulls.author: nikolaichuk7
pulls.body:
Twenty commits. The first seven are the seven items of my 22 September note, in the order that lets each refer to the one before; the next nine came from building the profile and running it on hardware against its own text; 17 to 19 are corrections from a full re-read of the profile against its own words, with the whole exercise re-run on the corrected code; 20 applies the review of 26 September, every comment in one commit, re-run on hardware. Rows 1 to 19 describe the commits as they were made; where commit 20 changed their result (`server_id` is now `rrp_id`, the absent-timestamp `handle` is back), row 20 says so. Each commit message says what was hard to turn into an edit and how the text resolves it. Where a decision is the authors' to make, the alternative is stated here rather than in the draft. The commits are kept apart so that each item can be reviewed on its own; they can be squashed on merge.

Section numbers are those of the draft as built from this branch.

| # | Commit | Item | Where | What the commit does | What it rests on | Decision for the SIG |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4c8b994 | Editorial | 5.1 (and anchors in 8.1, 9.1.3, 9.2.4) | One Method/Success/Response block instead of two; anchors for the structures the text refers to | — | none |
| 2 | 7ce5ab4 | Relationship to LAMPS work | 6 | How `attest-initiate` relates to `/est/nonce` of attestation-freshness-08 (Section 5.1: GET or POST, `application/est-attestation-freshness+json`, a nonce of 8 to 64 bytes, optional `expiry`), and how Evidence beside the CSR relates to csr-attestation-29 (the `id-aa-attestation` attribute, Section 4.3; the CA/RA validates the binding to the CSR's key, Section 6.1) | the two drafts as posted | keep `attest-initiate` (A, as written: it carries the mode, `server_id` and the algorithms) or profile `/est/nonce` for the present-nonce leg (B) |
| 3 | c4b7f78 | Platform forms | 9.1.4 | Direct / nested / provider-scoped, with the measured cases: the Azure paravisor fixes REPORT_DATA at boot; AWS SEV-SNP shared tenancy is VLEK-signed with CHIP_ID zero; Nitro, Google Cloud SEV-SNP and TDX are direct | reports and certificates in `nikolaichuk7/geoar-verifier` (`azure-cvm/`, `aws-vlek/`, `gcp-cvm/`, `aws-nitro/`) | whether the Verifier must report the form in Attestation Results (as written) or the CA infers it |
| 4 | bda1129 | Key Certification | 9.1.3; 12.2 | Where the claim can come from: not from a SEV-SNP report or a TDX TDREPORT, whose only guest-chosen content is a 64-octet field; only from a second Attesting Environment (vTPM, measured software) | AMD 56860 Tables 26 and 27; Intel TDX ABI Tables 3.46 and 3.48 (REPORTDATA, 64 octets, in REPORTMACSTRUCT); Linux 7.0 UAPI `sev-guest.h` (`user_data[SNP_REPORT_USER_DATA_SIZE]`, 64) and `tdx-guest.h` (`TDX_REPORTDATA_LEN`, 64) | none, unless you prefer to drop Key Certification from the list |
| 5 | 4819019 | Evidence-to-Server (the TLS 1.3 form of RFC 7030 §3.5) | 8.1; 9.1.3; 9.1.5; 9.1.6; 9.2.5; 12.1; Appendix A | Adds `server_id`; a binding requirement; a length-prefixed `binding_input` with SHA-512 for 64-octet fields; recomputation by the CA and the Vault; the server-substitution consideration; tls-exporter as the optional §3.5 form when the Attester is the EST Client; a test vector. This commit called the binding "Evidence-to-Target"; commit 15 gives it its right name and adds the binding that TACRA's Target needs | RFC 7030 §3.5 (tls-unique in the challenge-password); RFC 9266 (tls-unique is not defined for TLS 1.3); TACRA §7.2 (untrusted conduit) | `server_id` = URI origin (A, as written) or a CA identifier from the response (B); whether the binding input replaces `H(handle ‖ CSR)` of TheBankster/rats-tacra#1 (it should; that PR now binds the same four values and cites this profile for the encoding) |
| 6 | 64b3dea | Origin of the bundle | 9.2.4; 9.2.6; 12.2 | Requires origin authentication: HPKE `mode_auth` with `server_id` and `handle` in `info`, or a Vault signature over the container (CMS SignedData over EnvelopedData; COSE_Sign1 over COSE_Encrypt0); adds the Attester-side checks the draft did not have | RFC 9180 §5.1.3 (at most two parties can produce the shared secret; another identity for the sender belongs in `info`); RFC 5652; RFC 9052 | HPKE `mode_auth` (A) or a signature (B) as the mandatory one; both are in the text as alternatives |
| 7 | 23e2b8c | `expires_in` floor | 8.1; 8.1.1 | SHOULD NOT be below 60 s, with the measurement that sets it | `hatls` v0.3.0, `evidence/runtime-cost-20260922T153300Z/snp-burst.json`; commit 16 adds the cause and three more hosts | the number (60 s as written, or higher) |
| 8 | 4381822 | Analysis by role | 12.4 | What each of the five roles holds and can do, the check that bounds it, and which check closes which attack | the ProVerif model and the reference implementation in `nikolaichuk7/tacra-est` | none |
| 9 | 2365dbb | Envelopes in CDDL | 7.1 | CDDL for the four structures | attestation-freshness-08 Section 5.1 for the JSON `bstr` convention; validated with the `cddl` tool against the messages of a live SEV-SNP run, with two negative controls (`tacra-est/scripts/validate_cddl.py`) | the container names for CMS and COSE are placeholders until those profiles are written |
| 10 | a56ff68 | Example exchange | Appendix B | The messages of one enrollment and one retrieval, as produced with a live SEV-SNP Attester | regenerated in commit 16 | none |
| 11 | 36cfa03 | Handle Lifetime, second measurement | 8.1.1 | Superseded by commit 16. The figure it added, 163 ms per report, measured the reference implementation of that day, whose Attester downloaded AMD's certificate chain for every report; it said nothing about the platform | — | none |
| 12 | 368eb3f | Implementation Status | 11 | RFC 7942 section: the reference implementation, what it covers and what it does not | `nikolaichuk7/tacra-est` | the licence line reads "open source" until the repository's licence is chosen |
| 13 | 22d1ad9 | The TWI SIG implementation | 11 | Notes the SIG's implementation and the interop between the two | `tacra-est/interop/` | none |
| 14 | ee7a6a1 | Primary-source check | 9.1.3; 9.1.4; references | Every platform statement re-checked against the vendor documents and cited by table: AMD 56860 rev. 1.59 (Tables 26, 27, 51; Section 3.6), Intel TDX ABI 348551-008US (Tables 3.46 to 3.52; Section 5.5.10), Base Architecture 348549-008US (Table 12.1), the TDX DCAP Quote Library API. Corrected: SIGNING_KEY (not KEY_INFO); a TDX guest can also extend RTMRs and assign signer identities; a MASK_CHIP_KEY report is unsigned | the documents themselves | none |
| 15 | 0a7f9b3 | The Target, as TACRA defines it | 5.1; 7.1; 8.1; 9.1.1; 9.1.3; 9.1.5; 9.1.6; 9.2.1; 9.2.2; 9.2.4 to 9.2.6; 12.1; 12.4; Appendix A | `attest-initiate` takes `target` and `credential_type`; both legs carry them; the Target is bound in Evidence beside `server_id`; a server refuses a second leg whose Target or Credential Type differs from the initiation's. `server_id` names the EST Server; the Target is the RATS-unaware Relying Party (TACRA §2); binding `server_id` alone leaves Target substitution open | TACRA §2, §5.1 to §5.3 and Design Goal 5; ProVerif `enrollment-serveronly` (attack) and `enrollment-bind` (proof); drills D10 (issued for the wrong Target under -00) and D9 (refused) | none |
| 16 | e33f050 | Handle Lifetime from the primary sources; appendices from one run | 8.1.1; 11; Appendices A and B; references | The throttle is the one the GHCB specification recommends (§4.1.7) and the 2 s / 60 s retry is the Linux guest driver's; on every Google Cloud SEV-SNP guest measured, every tenth report requested back to back waits about 10.2 s, and the report itself takes 7.7 to 8.2 ms wherever it was timed alone; the 60 s floor is stated against the longest wait measured (10.4 s) and against the driver's own limit (about 62 s), which it does not cover. The Test Vector and the Example Exchange now come from one run, whose messages carry the Target and validate against the CDDL; the vector's SHA-512 digest equals REPORT_DATA of that run's report | AMD 56421 rev. 2.04 §4.1.7; Linux 7.0 `__handle_guest_request` and `SNP_REQ_RETRY_DELAY` / `SNP_REQ_MAX_RETRY_DURATION`; `tacra-est/evidence/`; superseded for the appendices by commit 18 | none |
| 17 | dd156ff | Nine text corrections | 8.1.1; 9.1.1; 9.2.1; 9.2.2; 9.2.5; 9.2.6; 11; 12.4; error handling; binding-input; CDDL | On re-reading: the binding input's freshness element is not empty for all absent-* kinds (it is the Handle for present-*, the epoch marker for absent-epoch); Retrieval now binds server_id and the Target as Enrollment does; plaintext re-encryption by the EST Server is forbidden (TACRA Goal 10), not merely discouraged; the binding CDDL admits the Evidence-to-CSR methods the prose lists; Implementation Status calls the interop what it is, behaviour not wire format; Attester Processing no longer checks a group_id the Attester never chose; Analysis by Role binds the Target for the CA and the Vault; the recompute is described from the corresponding attest-initiate, not a Handle the Relying Party issued; an expired present-nonce is 409 and the Attester retries | the draft against itself, TACRA §4.4/§5.4/§7.2 | HPKE `mode_auth` vs a Vault signature stays the SIG's to make; the algorithm field name (`hash` vs the TWI implementation's `hash_alg`) is for the SIG to reconcile |
| 18 | d65fba4 | Appendices from the corrected-code run | Appendices A and B | The Test Vector and the Example Exchange are regenerated from a run whose Attester makes no network request (code 9850c7dfe79e); the vector's SHA-512 digest equals REPORT_DATA of that run's report, recomputed independently | `tacra-est/evidence/20260926T202045Z-gcp-sev-snp/` | none |
| 19 | 0f6e2cc | Handle Lifetime wording | 8.1.1 | Count-free phrasing, since a fifth SEV-SNP run shares a chip with an earlier one | the runs | none |
| 20 | fa4cd72 | Review of 26 September | 6; 7.1; 8.1; 8.1.1 (new); 8.1.2; 9.1.1; 9.1.3; 9.1.5; 9.1.6; 9.2.1; 9.2.2; 9.2.4 to 9.2.6; 10; 11; 12; Appendices A and B | Evidence is produced for a Verifier or an RRP, never for an EST Server: `server_id` becomes `rrp_id`, the RRP that relies on the Evidence (the CA for Enrollment, the Vault for Retrieval); item 4 is Evidence-to-RRP; each RRP recomputes with its own identifier; the Attester no longer compares identifiers, it binds the one its CAI holds, or else the response's. absent-timestamp: `handle` carries the Attester's timestamp again (8 octets, seconds since 1970, RFC 7519 NumericDate) and the binding input takes it; `max_age` is a requirement on the RRP. One binding method: the five requirements apply together, the binding input meets items 2 to 5, the other three methods only in addition. Fewer options: csr-attestation an optional path; HPKE `mode_auth` the one mandatory container; a subsection on what is advertised and what is agreed. The Retrieval sentence in 6 is scoped to Enrollment; Handle Lifetime is the requirement and one line of why. Security: freshness that is not single-use; the clock behind absent-timestamp. Implementation Status: the cases run against the SIG's code were key substitution and bundle substitution, not server substitution as the text said | the review comments; ProVerif, 24 models (`tacra-est/formal/`), among them 15 on where the bound identity comes from under five sources of freshness; drills D1 to D21 on SEV-SNP run 20260926T234654Z | whether the Attester MUST hold the RRP identifier or MAY take it from the response (the TODO in 8.1); whether `credential_type` is carried on the wire; the names `acceptable_evidence` and `profile` |

Corrections to my 22 September note, found while checking every claim: the csr-attestation attribute is `id-aa-attestation` in -29, not `id-aa-evidence`; and the 300 s nonce lifetime I mentioned, which I first dropped because I could not re-verify it, is now verified in the SIG implementation's source (`internal/mockca/attest.go`, `nonceLifetime`) and cited in 8.1.1.

The hardware run behind the appendices, in one paragraph. Google Cloud `n2d-standard-2` (EPYC Milan, SEV firmware 1.58 build 1, SEV-SNP active), code at `tacra-est` e116768fe989, run 20260926T234654Z. The Attester makes no network request: it takes the VCEK, ASK and ARK from the host's certificate table. The report is VCEK-signed; its signature and the VCEK → ASK → ARK chain verify with OpenSSL, and the pinned ARK is DER-identical to the ARK-Milan that AMD's KDS serves. REPORT_DATA equals the SHA-512 digest of the binding input (Handle, `rrp_id`, Target, CSR; 320 octets), recomputed independently from the test vector. All 23 drills behave as on the mock: honest enrollment and retrieval in all five Freshness Kinds, including `attest-initiate` completed locally; a moved epoch answered 409 and the retry issued; a timestamp older than `max_age` answered 409; RRP substitution and Target substitution refused with `binding-mismatch` under this text and issued under -00; with the RRP identifier taken from the response instead of held, the conduit's choice of RRP issues (D3b), as the ProVerif model predicts; one `absent-timestamp` request refused at a second RRP under this text and issued by both CAs under -00; bundle substitution refused by the Attester under this text and accepted under -00; a replayed Handle answered 409. D10's report met the host's throttle and took 10.2 s, the wait the Handle Lifetime floor is for. Verifier time on the server 31.1 ms median; the enrollment request is 17 395 bytes with the certificate chain inside the Evidence. All seven messages validate against the CDDL, and the three negative controls are refused.

The draft builds with the repository's Makefile (kramdown-rfc 1.7.43, xml2rfc 3.34.1); the two "both inline and in YAML header" notes for RFC 7030 and RFC 9334 pre-date this PR.

Artifact: `nikolaichuk7/tacra-est` holds the twenty-four ProVerif models with their output, the reference implementation (Attester, honest and dishonest conduits, EST Server with the three resources and all five Freshness Kinds, Verifier for SEV-SNP and a mock, CA, Vault with HPKE `mode_auth`), the drills, the CDDL check, and the raw evidence of every run with the SHA-256 sums taken on the VM.

## Interop with the TWI SIG implementation

The SIG's own EST fork (`TWI-Unified-Model/globalsign-est`) is a second, independent implementation. Both carry the Target and the Credential Type as the `target` and `credential_type` query parameters of `attest-initiate`, and both choose the mode, enrollment or retrieval, by a per-Target policy. Running our findings against it, through its public Go API, confirms both cases in its own code (`tacra-est/interop/`, `RESULTS.txt`):

- The `csr-hash` binding is declared and its presence required, but `CSRHash()` is never called on the verify path and the mock EAT omits the CSR, so a swapped CSR is issued a certificate (key substitution).
- `SealCredentialBundle` needs only CEKpub and `Open` does not check the sender, so a bundle sealed by no Vault is accepted (bundle substitution).

Both are the expected state of a declared POC — its own comment names HPKE as "the baseline the specification will ultimately mandate" — and the tests turn that into a reproducing case. This is contributed as interop, not as a vulnerability report.

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body:
Pushed fa4cd72, which applies this review in one commit (so the threads above now show as outdated). By thread:

- `server_id` / Evidence produced for an EST Server: it is now `rrp_id`, the RRP that relies on the Evidence (the CA for Enrollment, the Vault for Retrieval); item 4 is Evidence-to-RRP, and the Attester no longer compares identifiers. Which source is required, held or taken from the response, is a TODO in 8.1 for Tuesday.
- absent-timestamp: your rule is back. The timestamp travels in `handle` as 8 octets, seconds since 1970, and the binding input takes it.
- Where the bindings are specified, and exclusive or additive: `evidence` points to the binding input (9.1.5); the five requirements apply together; `binding-input` is the one method, and the other three are only in addition.
- Options: csr-attestation is an optional path, HPKE `mode_auth` is the one mandatory container, and a new 8.1.1 says what is advertised and what is agreed out of band.
- The Retrieval sentence is scoped to Enrollment; Handle Lifetime keeps the requirement and one line of why.
- Left for you: `credential_type` on the wire, and the `acceptable_evidence` / `profile` names.

Also fixed in passing: Implementation Status said the interop with the SIG's code reproduced server substitution; what it reproduced was key substitution and bundle substitution.

The reference implementation now runs all five Freshness Kinds. It was re-run on SEV-SNP (run 20260926T234654Z): all 23 drills behaved as expected, and the appendices are regenerated from that run ([RESULTS](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/main/docs/RESULTS.md)). The ProVerif set is now 24 models, adding Verifier-issued Handles and the absent-timestamp case ([formal/README.md](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/main/formal/README.md)). TheBankster/rats-tacra#1 carries the same change to the binding text.

This is not strictly correct; "target" might be a parameter, but Credential Type is (currently) not. It's left to retrieve/enroll phases. This is illustrated here: https://github.com/TWI-Unified-Model/tacra/blob/main/proto/initiate.mmd
It is of course possible that this is a mistake, which then needs to be corrected in the TACRA PoC as well.

The expanded capabilities are noteworthy and likely useful, but they also introduce complexity and a need to either negotiate things or configure them out of band. We should discuss and document what needs to happen.

Thanks, Mark — fast turnaround, appreciated.

I put `credential_type` on `attest-initiate` because two of the sources I was working from carry it there: Section 5.1 of the TACRA draft lists "Credential Type" as an Initiate-Credential-Acquisition parameter and says Initiate validates that the Target, Credential Type and Hint are supported by the CAS; and the TWI reference server sends it on initiate (`attestCredentialTypeParam` in `attest_client.go`). So the profile followed those.

`initiate.mmd` is in a repo I can't open, so I'll defer to it. If the intended model is that only `target` is on the first call and Credential Type is settled in the enroll/retrieve phase, I'll make `credential_type` second-leg only: drop it from the `attest-initiate` query and from the "must equal the initiate" check, keeping the Target match. The binding input never included Credential Type, so nothing else changes. As you note, TACRA Section 5.1 and the PoC's initiate call would then want the same tweak.

Either way is a small edit; tell me which and I'll align the draft and the reference implementation.

Agreed — useful, and it does add complexity. Part of the negotiation surface is already in the profile: the `attest-initiate` response carries `acceptable_evidence` and `acceptable_csk` / `acceptable_cek`, and the `binding` object names the Evidence-to-CSR method, so a server can advertise what it accepts and the client can pick. What isn't written yet is the configuration/policy side: whether a Credential Authority requires csr-attestation inside the CSR in addition to the Evidence beside it, and how that requirement is signalled. I can add a short "negotiation and configuration" note — here and in 9.1.3 — stating what the initiate response advertises and what has to be agreed out of band. Good topic for Tuesday; I'll draft the text whichever way you want it to land.
I would rephrase it. Evidence requirements for Enroll vs. Retrieve are entirely separate, so this sentence reads weird.

My instinct is to specify something rather than leave too much to the implementer, so long as doing so doesn't lock anything major out. We can always add (necessary) complexity later. Too many options at once without at least some validation that each one is actually necessary is a dangerous path to take.

Agreed — that sentence mixes the two modes. This paragraph is about Enrollment's choice between Evidence in the CSR and beside it; Retrieval has no CSR and its Evidence carries CEKpub by construction (Section 9.2.2), which is a separate matter and doesn't belong in the same breath.

I'll drop the trailing sentence and, if it reads better, scope the paragraph explicitly to Enrollment — e.g. after "...a Credential Authority MAY require either or both": "This choice is specific to Enrollment; Retrieval has no CSR and binds Evidence to CEKpub (Section 9.2.2)."

I'll fold this into the revision together with the other two points rather than push it mid-review, so you get one clean update.
This is nowhere in TACRA. Should this be added there?

Agreed, and I'd rather cut than caveat. Concretely, on what's optional here and where it came from:

- The three Evidence-to-CSR methods (CSR Hash, Public Key Thumbprint, Key Certification) are inherited from the base draft's "at least one of". I'd make `binding-input` the single MUST — it is the one specified end to end and validated on hardware — and drop or demote the other two.
- The csr-attestation "either or both" is mine. I'll reduce it to: this profile carries Evidence beside the CSR, and placing attestations in the CSR per csr-attestation is an optional interop path, not a co-equal requirement.
- For the bundle, one mandatory container (HPKE `mode_auth`) instead of the CMS / COSE menu, with the others listed as optional.

That leaves one specified way through Enrollment and one through Retrieval, everything else explicitly optional. Tell me if that's the line you want and I'll write it that way — good to lock on Tuesday.

Good catch — and yes, it belongs in TACRA. PR #1 there (branch binding-to-evidence) already adds it: the freshness input binds four values — the Freshness Handle, "an identifier of the credential-acquisition service that the CAI is configured to use for the Target, such as the origin of an EST Server's URI", the Target, and the CSR or CEKpub. `server_id` in this profile is the EST spelling of that generic service-identifier element, so the two drafts are consistent by construction.

If the TACRA PR wording doesn't make it obvious that `server_id` here is the same element, I'll tighten it there so the mapping is explicit.

This may very well be a security requirement, but currently TACRA does not imbue the Attester with any knowledge of what the Server ID is. In fact, CAS is intended to be fully transparent to the Attester, client and server both. RRP (RATS Relying Party) and Verifier need not be, but we should still talk about what Attester needs to enforce as far as who it generates Evidence for. This should be discussed next Tuesday.

Agreed — that sentence asks the Attester to know something TACRA deliberately keeps from it, and it turns out not to be needed.

I checked before answering. I re-ran the model with the Attester-side comparison removed ([formal/enrollment-bind-nocompare.pv](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/main/formal/enrollment-bind-nocompare.pv)): the Attester no longer looks at the `server_id` it receives through the CAS; it binds the server identity it holds, and every server recomputes the binding with its own. All three enrollment queries still hold ([results](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/main/formal/results/proverif-20260926T224122Z.txt)). So the comparison was defence in depth, not what carries the guarantee, and I'll drop the "Attester MUST compare `server_id`" sentence.

What remains, and I agree it's for Tuesday: the value that gets bound has to come from inside the Attester's trust boundary, not from the CAS. TACRA already has the CAI select the mechanism per Target (Design Goal 5), so the CAI's per-Target configuration is the natural source. If the intent is that even that stays out of the Attester's view, then server substitution is prevented only where that identity is configured, and the text should say so. I'll bring both options.
Does this level of detail belong in an IETF I-D? Should we find another home for it? I don't want to lose it, and I don't think its place is here.

Fair — I'd move it. The draft only needs the requirement and one line of why; the platform specifics (the GHCB rate-limit recommendation, the Linux driver's retry constants, the Google Cloud timings) are evidence, not protocol.

Proposed text for this subsection:

> Producing hardware Evidence can be delayed: a platform may rate-limit attestation requests, so an Attester can wait several seconds for the report that carries the Handle. A Handle originator SHOULD NOT set `expires_in` below 60 s; the measurements that motivate the value are in {{TACRA-EST-IMPL}}.

The full detail already lives in the tacra-est repo ([docs/RESULTS.md](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/main/docs/RESULTS.md), section 4, every source cited), so nothing is lost; the draft just points there. If you'd rather it sit somewhere the WG maintains — the RATS wiki that came up at the interim, or the TWI repo — I can write it up for either.
If credential_type ends up not carried one the wire, as I suspect it won't, then this will need to be reworded.
I thought for absent-timestamp, the handle is the attester's timestamp. Is that not so?
Where are these bindings specified so the implementer knows what do implement?

Understood, and I expect the same. For the record, your original text had it OPTIONAL in the retrieval request only; I made it REQUIRED in both requests to mirror TACRA Sections 5.2-5.3.

If Credential Type stays a CAAPI parameter (CAI to EST Client) and isn't carried in EST, the rewording is contained:

- remove `credential_type` from both request bodies, from `request-common` in the CDDL and from the examples, together with the "MUST equal the preceding `attest-initiate`" clauses; `target` and its match stay;
- add one sentence: the EST Server determines what to mint or release from the Target and its own policy, and the Attester side checks that what comes back is the Credential Type it asked for (for Retrieval that is the CAI after unwrapping, since the CAS never sees inside the bundle).

Two things follow from it, worth settling in the same decision:

1. TACRA Sections 5.1-5.3 list an Unsupported (5.3: Invalid) Credential Type failure. With no type on the wire, the EST Server can't detect it; the CAS Client can, from its own configuration. One sentence in TACRA saying which side checks would keep the two documents consistent.
2. In the TWI globalsign-est fork, the mock CA's `TargetPolicy` allows a list of Credential Types per Target, and its check runs only when a request carries a type (the field is already optional in all three messages there). With nothing on the wire, a Target that allows two types in the same mode, e.g. JWT and API key, both by retrieval, has no way to say which. The simplest rule is one Credential Type per Target and mode, fixed by CAS policy.

I'll fold this into the same revision as your first comment.
Should "acceptable_evidence" then be renamed to "acceptable_profiles"? Otherwise it's not intuitive that one corresponds to the other. Maybe then this can be renamed into "chosen_profile".
Noting something you're like to fix already: Evidence is never produced for an EST Server, only for a Verifier or RRP.
Are these mutually exclusive or additive?

You're right, and my edit broke it. I made `handle` absent for absent-timestamp on the reasoning that the timestamp is a claim inside Evidence, like an EAT `iat`. On a direct-form platform that doesn't hold: an SEV-SNP report has no time field, and REPORT_DATA is the only value the guest chooses, so a timestamp that isn't in the binding input isn't covered by the report's signature at all. absent-timestamp would then give no freshness on exactly the platform we measured. Our implementation exercises present-nonce only, which is why no run caught it.

So I'll restore your rule: `handle` REQUIRED unless `absent-none`, carrying the Attester's timestamp for absent-timestamp, and the binding input takes it like any other freshness element. One detail to fix for interop, since the Relying Party recomputes the binding input byte for byte: the timestamp's encoding. I'd propose an 8-octet big-endian unsigned count of seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z (the NumericDate of JWT and CWT), which the Verifier compares against `max_age`.

In this draft: "Key Binding and PoP Requirements" (`{{key-binding}}` is its anchor) says what must be bound, and "Binding Input" right after it gives the construction: the octet string, its SHA-512 digest in the 64-octet report field, and how the Credential Authority or Secret Vault recomputes it. The appendix "Test Vector for the Binding Input" works one through end to end, and Retrieval reuses the construction with CEKpub as the subject ("Evidence-to-CEK Binding").

Your question does expose a gap, though. An implementer reading the requirements meets three Evidence-to-CSR methods (CSR Hash, Public Key Thumbprint, Key Certification) and a `binding.method` field, and nothing there says that `binding-input` is the method that meets the requirements in one go; the Binding Input section is also scoped to the direct platform form only. In short: an identifier that comes through the CAS keeps any one Evidence to one RRP. That matters when freshness isn't per-RRP (the shared-epoch rows); with a per-RRP Handle, the Handle already does it. Only a configured identifier makes it the RRP the deployment intended. And with a local `attest-initiate` there is no response to take the identifier from, so configuration is the only source there.
